faqs.q: Which eCommerce platform do you use?
faqs.a: The one that fits your products, budget and team: an established platform such as WooCommerce or Shopify, or a custom build for complex catalogs or B2B ordering. We explain the trade-offs before you decide.

faqs.q: Can you move our existing store to a new platform?
faqs.a: Yes. We move products, customers and order history, and set up redirects so you keep your search rankings.

faqs.q: Will the store work well on phones?
faqs.a: Yes. We design mobile-first, because most shoppers browse and buy on their phones, and test checkout on real devices.

faqs.q: How do you keep payments secure?
faqs.a: We use trusted payment providers, so card details never touch your server, plus HTTPS, security hardening and daily backups.

faqs.q: Can the store connect to our inventory or accounting system?
faqs.a: Yes. Common connections include ERP, accounting, CRM, shipping and email tools, so orders, stock and invoices stay in sync.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a website and a web application?
faqs.a: A website mainly shares information. A web application lets people do work: sign in, fill in forms, approve requests, manage records and see reports.

faqs.q: Can it connect to the software we already use?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Most business tools offer APIs, and we map the connections you need during planning.

faqs.q: Will it work on phones and tablets?
faqs.a: Yes. We build responsive web apps that work in any modern browser, so staff can use them in the office or in the field.

faqs.q: How do you keep our data secure?
faqs.a: Secure logins, role-based access, encryption, audit logs and regular backups are part of the build, not an add-on.

faqs.q: Can we start small?
faqs.a: Yes. We often start with one process as a first release, then add features in sprints based on feedback from your team.

faqs.q: Should we use WordPress or a headless CMS?
faqs.a: WordPress suits most websites and gives editors a familiar interface. A headless CMS suits teams that publish the same content to a website, an app and other channels. We recommend one based on your content and team.

faqs.q: Can you move our content from our current system?
faqs.a: Yes. We migrate pages, posts, images and links, and set up redirects so visitors and search engines find the new pages.

faqs.q: Will we need a developer for everyday changes?
faqs.a: No. Editors can add pages, change text and images and publish posts on their own. Developers are only needed for new features or layouts.

faqs.q: Can several people edit with approvals?
faqs.a: Yes. We set up roles so some people draft, others review, and only approved content goes live.

faqs.q: How do you keep the CMS secure?
faqs.a: We keep the core and plugins to what you need, apply updates, set strong logins and roles, and run daily backups.

faqs.q: How do we know if our website needs a redesign?
faqs.a: Common signs are slow pages, a poor layout on phones, an outdated look, fewer leads than you'd expect, or a site your team finds hard to update. Our health check shows which of these apply.

faqs.q: Will we lose our search rankings?
faqs.a: Not if the relaunch is planned well. We keep or redirect every important page, carry over titles and descriptions, and check search performance after launch.

faqs.q: Can you keep our brand and content?
faqs.a: Yes. We can work within your current brand and reuse content that still works, or refresh both if you want a bigger change.

faqs.q: Do we have to redesign everything at once?
faqs.a: No. We can start with the pages that matter most, such as the homepage and service pages, then improve the rest in stages.

faqs.q: Can you write the copy as well?
faqs.a: Yes. We offer tone-of-voice and copywriting support, so the words and design work together.

faqs.q: What is a web portal?
faqs.a: A secure area of your website where signed-in users, such as customers, partners or staff, see information and complete tasks meant only for them.

faqs.q: Who can use the portal?
faqs.a: Anyone you invite. We set up roles so each type of user sees only their own data and the features they need.

faqs.q: How do you keep portal data secure?
faqs.a: Secure logins with two-factor authentication where needed, role-based access, encryption, audit logs and regular backups.

faqs.q: Can the portal connect to our existing systems?
faqs.a: Yes. Common connections include CRM, ERP, billing and document storage, so information stays in sync without double entry.

faqs.q: Will it work on phones?
faqs.a: Yes. We design portals mobile-first and test them on real devices and browsers.
